en: Thus have I heard: the Cūḷapuṇṇamasutta (The Shorter Discourse on the Full-Moon Night), Majjhima Nikāya 110.
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Eastern Park, in the Mansion of Migāra’s Mother.
Now on that occasion, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth, during the full moon night, the Blessed One was seated in the open air surrounded by the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
Then the Blessed One, having surveyed the silent Saṅgha of bhikkhus again and again, addressed the bhikkhus:
“Bhikkhus, would an untrue person know an untrue person, thinking:
‘This person is an untrue person’?
“Certainly not, Bhante.”
“Excellent, bhikkhus!
It is impossible, bhikkhus, it is out of the question that an untrue man should know an untrue man:
‘This person is an untrue man.’”
“But would an untrue person, bhikkhus, know a true person thus:
‘This venerable one is a true person’?
“Certainly not, Bhante.”
“Excellent, bhikkhus!
This too, bhikkhus, is impossible, it cannot happen, that a person of inferior character should know a person of superior character:
‘This person is a person of superior character.’”
“Monks, an untrue person is one who possesses the qualities of an untrue person, who has the devotion of an untrue person, who has the thoughts of an untrue person,
who has the counsel of an untrue person, who has the speech of an untrue person, who has the actions of an untrue person, who has the views of an untrue person,
and who gives the gifts of an untrue person.”
And how, monks, is an untrue person possessed of bad qualities?
Here, monks, an untrue person is faithless, shameless, reckless, of little learning, lazy, muddled in mindfulness, and lacking wisdom.
It is in this way, monks, that an untrue person is possessed of bad qualities.
And how, monks, is an untrue man one who associates with untrue men?

Here, monks, those ascetics and brahmins who are faithless, shameless, unafraid of wrongdoing, unlearned, lazy, muddled in mindfulness, and lacking wisdom—they are his friends, they are his companions.
It is in this way, monks, that an untrue man is one who associates with untrue men.
And how, monks, is an untrue man one who thinks the thoughts of an untrue man?
Here, monks, an untrue man intends for his own affliction, he intends for the affliction of others, and he intends for the affliction of both.
It is in this way, monks, that an untrue man is one who thinks the thoughts of an untrue man.
And how, monks, is an untrue person one who consults with an untrue person?
Here, monks, an untrue person consults for his own harm, consults for the harm of others, and consults for the harm of both.
It is in this way, monks, that an untrue person is one who consults with an untrue person.
And how, monks, is an untrue person one whose speech is that of an untrue person?
Here, monks, an untrue person is a speaker of falsehood, a speaker of malicious speech, a speaker of harsh speech, and a gossip.
It is in this way, monks, that an untrue person is one whose speech is that of an untrue person.
And how, monks, is an untrue man one whose actions are those of an untrue man?
Here, monks, an untrue man is a destroyer of life, a taker of what is not given, and one who engages in sexual misconduct.
It is in this way, monks, that an untrue man is one whose actions are those of an untrue man.
And how, monks, does an untrue person hold the view of an untrue person?
Here, monks, an untrue person holds such a view as this:
"There is no gift, there is no offering, there is no oblation; there is no fruit or result of deeds well done or ill done."
‘There is no result of kamma; there is no this world, there is no other world; there is no mother, there is no father;

there are no beings who arise spontaneously; there are in the world no ascetics or brahmins who have attained the right path and practiced rightly, who having realized this world and the other world for themselves by direct knowledge, make them known to others.’”
In this way, monks, an untrue person has the view of an untrue person.
And how, monks, does an untrue person give an untrue gift? Here, monks, an untrue person gives a gift without respect;
he gives a gift not with his own hand; he gives a gift without treating it with reverence; he gives a gift that is thrown away; he gives a gift holding the view of non-return.
In this way, monks, an untrue person gives the gift of an untrue person. Such an untrue person, monks,
being thus possessed of unrighteous qualities, thus devoted to the company of untrue persons, thus thinking like an untrue person, thus plotting like an untrue person,
thus speaking like an untrue person, and thus acting like an untrue person—
Such is the view of a person who is not a true man;
having given such a gift, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the destination of those who are not true men.
And what, monks, is the destination of those who are not true men?
“Or hell, or the animal realm.
Would a true person, monks, know a true person thus:
‘This venerable one is a true person’?”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“Good, monks.
It is possible, monks, that a true person might recognize a true person:”
“‘This person is a true man,’ one might know.
But could one, monks, know an untrue man: ‘This person is not a true man’?”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“Good, monks.
This too is a possibility, monks, that a true man might know an untrue man:”
‘This person is not a true man. Monks,

a true man is one who possesses the true Dhamma, who honors the true man, who thinks like a true man, who counsels like a true man, who speaks like a true man, who acts like a true man, who holds the views of a true man, and who gives the gift of a true man.
And how, monks, is a true person endowed with the true Dhamma?
Here, monks, a true person is endowed with faith, possessed of a sense of shame, possessed of moral dread, learned, energetic, established in mindfulness, and wise.
It is in this way, monks, that a true person is endowed with the true Dhamma.
And how, monks, does a true person honor a true person?

Here, monks, those ascetics and brahmins who possess faith, a sense of shame, moral dread, great learning, aroused energy, established mindfulness, and wisdom—these are his friends, these are his companions.
It is in this way, monks, that a true person honors a true person.
And how, monks, is a true person one who thinks like a true person?
Here, monks, a true person does not intend for his own harm, nor does he intend for the harm of others, nor does he intend for the harm of both.
It is in this way, monks, that a true person is one who thinks like a true person.
And how, monks, is a true person one who consults with true persons?
Here, monks, a true person does not consult for his own harm, nor does he consult for the harm of others, nor does he consult for the harm of both.
It is in this way, monks, that a true person is one who consults with true persons.
And how, monks, is a true man one whose speech is that of a true man?
Here, monks, a true man abstains from false speech, abstains from malicious speech, abstains from harsh speech, and abstains from idle chatter.
It is in this way, monks, that a true man is one whose speech is that of a true man.
And how, monks, is a true person one whose actions are those of a true person?
Here, monks, a true person abstains from the destruction of life, abstains from taking what is not given, and abstains from sexual misconduct.
It is in this way, monks, that a true person is one whose actions are those of a true person.
And how, monks, does a true person have the view of a true person?
Here, monks, a true person has such a view as this: ‘There is what is given;
there is what is offered; there is what is sacrificed; there is the fruit and result of deeds well done and ill done.’
‘There is kamma and its result; there is this world and the other world; there is mother and father; there are beings of spontaneous birth;

and there are in the world ascetics and brahmins who have attained the right path and practiced rightly, who, having realized this world and the other world for themselves through direct knowledge, make them known.’”
In this way, monks, a true person possesses the view of a true person.
And how, monks, does a true person give the gift of a true person?

Here, monks, a true person gives a gift respectfully; he gives a gift with his own hand; he gives a gift with a sense of esteem; he gives a gift without disdain; and he gives a gift with the conviction that there is a future life.
In this way, monks, a true person gives the gift of a true person.
Such a true person, monks, is thus endowed with the true Dhamma, thus devoted to true persons, thus thinking like a true person, thus consulting like a true person,
thus speaking like a true person, thus acting like a true person, and thus possessing the view of a true person.
Having given such a gift of a true person, with the breakup of the body, after death, one is reborn in the destination of true persons.
And what, bhikkhus, is the destination of true persons?
It is either greatness among the devas or greatness among human beings.”
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
The monks were delighted and rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The Cūḷapuṇṇamasutta, the tenth, is finished.
The first chapter, the Devadaha Vagga, is finished.
Its summary verse (uddāna) is:
Devadaha, the group of five.
Kinti Sāma, Sunakkhatta,
Sappāya, Gaṇa, Gopaka,
Mahāpuṇṇa, and Cūḷapuṇṇa.
